defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The frozen semantics contract's S1 entry carries retention_status RETAINED_BY_COMPLETED_REPRESENTATIVE_M1F0_EVENT and no sha256 field. Independent machine-wide search (all 24576-byte files under the coding and data roots, 151 candidates hashed) found no retained byte payload matching the banked S1 identity 8309377ee8e8f34eb91cdb025624144eb5be7821ed9e4a295df29b13aac5a0dd; only the hash is committed (m1f0 stage_sha256.post_attention_residual) plus retained payloads sufficient for zero-reread deterministic reproduction per the banked reproduction bundle. This matches project doctrine (F_norm was likewise hash-only before its dedicated materialization authority) and S2 is prohibited and NOT_YET_COMPUTED here, so nothing in this package is invalidated, and any future S2 authority pinning the S1 hash fails closed. Recommend an append-only clarification binding S1's sha256 and distinguishing BYTE_RETAINED from HASH_RETAINED_REPRODUCIBLE before any S2-phase authority cites this line.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: S1_RETENTION_STATUS_IS_HASH_RETENTION_NOT_BYTE_RETENTION

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: preflight_and_consume trusts the caller-supplied authorization object for expected sha256, manifest identity, and geometry; only the separate validator pins the committed authorization bytes (and pins the resolver sha). A consumer invoking the resolver with a mutated in-memory document could target different bytes. Mitigated: the committed authorization is hash-pinned by the validator and preparation evidence, exactly one machine-local copy of the aggregate exists, and downstream execution requires separate authority. Recommend future consumers be required to run the committed validator (repo mode) and hash-match the authorization file before calling the resolver, or add a self-identity gate to the next resolver version.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: RESOLVER_DOES_NOT_SELF_BIND_SUPPLIED_AUTHORIZATION_DOCUMENT

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The resolver compares fstat dev/ino before and after re-read on the same open descriptor; these are equal by construction and add no defense. The effective open-once protections are O_NOFOLLOW, regular-file/nlink-1/read-only checks, and BEFORE==CONSUMED==AFTER sha equality from the same descriptor, all present and tested. Cosmetic only.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: TAUTOLOGICAL_SAME_DESCRIPTOR_DEV_INO_COMPARISON

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Resolver tests omit a hard-link-alias case (nlink 2), a manifest-binding-mismatch case (manifest entry sha/path/role disagreeing with the authorization), and a wrong-manifest-byte-length case; the validator does not check the top-level schema string of the reuse authorization. All corresponding runtime checks exist in code and the 23 committed mutation cases plus 5 resolver cases passed live (7/7), so these are coverage hardening only.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: TEST_AND_VALIDATOR_COVERAGE_GAPS

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The three retained shared-expert packed weight payloads (verified byte-exact this review: gate 750b148a..., up 13727df9..., down 48c5469b..., all 0400 regular nlink-1) live in a machine-local retention package outside the committed repository whose parent directories are owner-writable, so unlink-and-replace or deletion is possible before the future weight-reuse authority consumes them. The consume-what-you-validated pattern (hash pinning at consume time) fails closed on substitution, and deletion would merely force a shard re-read under explicit new authority rather than silent corruption. Recommend the future REPRESENTATIVE_SHARED_EXPERT_RECOVERY_AUTHORIZATION re-verify EXPECTED==BEFORE==CONSUMED==AFTER on all three payloads from single descriptors, as this package already does for the aggregate.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: HISTORICAL_SHEXP_WEIGHT_PACKAGE_PARENT_DIRECTORY_WRITABLE
